title: Retinal vein changes after treatment with aflibercept and PRP in high-risk proliferative diabetic retinopathy

license.statement: CC BY 4.0 (article <license>: Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY))

condition: High-risk proliferative diabetic retinopathy in type 2 diabetes, no prior photocoagulation, anti-VEGF or steroid; retrospective single-arm cohort (59 patients, 59 eyes) treated January 2018 to December 2019; presence of centre-involving diabetic macular edema is not stated in the Methods

groups.agent: aflibercept 2 mg intravitreal (monthly for 3 months, then PRN, '3 + PRN') plus panretinal photocoagulation (532 nm laser, four sessions), PRP starting 1 week after the first injection
groups.description: All eyes of the retrospective cohort (one eye per patient)

exclusions.reason: test statistics and p-values are not admissible
same eyes and same baseline as Table 3 column 2 (duplicate); Table 3 cited

notes: Treatment schedule (Methods): aflibercept plus PRP at months 0, 1 and 2 (3 + PRN), further combination therapy if neovascularization persisted or recurred; number of injections not extracted
Indication coded 'other' (high-risk PDR) because the Methods do not state centre-involving diabetic macular edema
Fundus angiography used Heidelberg Spectralis HRA; thickness was measured on Cirrus HD-OCT

series.notes: Central foveal thickness (CFT, um) by Zeiss Cirrus HD-OCT built-in software, no subfield definition; mean ± SD (Methods: continuous variables expressed as mean ± SD); Table 3 row label gives n = 59; per-visit n not reported separately (paired t-tests against pre-treatment); months are 'months post-treatment' read as time since the first treatment
